text.p: CAI Wireless Systems Inc said Wednesday it has renegotiated an option to repurchase the $100 million face amount of CAI securities held by Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp.
CAI said it estimates the new option will result in cash savings of up to $100 million, depending on the timing of the repurchase.

The new repurchase consideration is $40 million in cash and 100,000 shares of convertible junior preferred, CAI said. The non-voting junior preferred has no maturity and is convertible into 2.5 million CAI common shares.
The consideration is an option exercisable through February 28, 1998, which requires the consent of holders of CAI's 12-1/4 percent senior notes due 2002, it said.
Spokesman Jason Thompson said CAI renegotiated the right to repurchase term notes due May 9, 2005, and 7,000 shares of senior preferred, a voting stock.
In return for the modification, the company said, it will withdraw its oposition to the Bell Atlantic/NYNEX merger.
CAI said the arrangement is an amendment of the so-called modification agreement entered into with Bell Atlantic and NYNEX last December.

Under the December agreement, which suspended the three companies' digital television venture, CAI only had a right to repurchase its securities at a premium above par that increased over time, it noted.

As a part of the amendment, NYNEX and Bell Atlantic also released CAI from its obligation under the digital TV agreement to make its wireless MMDS -- multichannel multipoint distribution system -- spectrum available to the phone companies at a future date in Boston, Pittsburgh, Albany, N.Y., Syracuse, N.Y., and Buffalo.
Upon a repurchase of the CAI securities, as contemplated by the amendment, the digital TV pact would lapse in its entirety, releasing a similar obligation in CAI's other markets, the company said.

NYNEX and Bell Atlantic also suspended or released CAI from a number of covenant restrictions and governance rights and provided CAI with a blanket proxy on their about 10 percent interest in CS Wireless Systems Inc, CAI's joint venture MMDS company with Heartland Wireless Communications Inc. If the repurchase were completed, the CS Wireless shares would be returned to CAI without further consideration.
The amendment also provides for a current mutual exchange of releases and an agreement to share certain patent and intellectual property rights related to their digital wireless venture.

CAI said the junior preferred it contemplates issuing to the two companies carries a liquidation preference of $30 million but carries no special dividends, covenants or governance rights. Each of the 100,000 shares of junior preferred is convertible into 25 CAI common shares in the hands of a subsequent purchaser unrelated to the two phone companies.

If the junior preferred stock continued to be held by the two companies at the end of three years and the value of the CAI common were not at least $14.00 per share, then they would be entitled to a value floor representing the difference between the then-market value of the CAI common and $14.00 per share. At CAI's election, the value floor would be payable either in the form of up to, but not more than, one million additional CAI common shares or a 10-year subordinated note in a principal amount of up to $15 million, bearing interest at eight percent, payable in kind for the first five years.
CAI said it does not expect to seek approval from senior note holders before this Fall, and only in connection with other financing arrangements.
The company noted it expects to close in the next several weeks the $30 million interim debt facility previously announced. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
